column1562:
22/Jul/26 7:47 PM;5f3432cde115420046434665;[~accountid:712020:f9a894b1-f824-4a33-a40d-1d507fe78d86] translating specific inks to Names and to RGB (web) colors is always a bit of science mixed with a bit of art mixed with a bit of hocus pocus.

These “greenish” colors are being reported as Black because they have low HSL brightness. With this low brightness, the hue is never being considered. 

So I’ve changed this to consider “Saturation” as well, based on some suggestions from Claude. With that in place, the file in question would have reported 1 instance of White and three instances of a very-similar-but-technically-different “Cyan.” 

“Why not green?” you ask?

{quote}At ~161°, your color falls into the 135–195 range, which is mapped to "Cyan". That is technically correct in HSL terms — (0, 71, 49) is a dark blue-green/teal, which sits closer to cyan than pure green on the color wheel (pure green is 120°).{quote}

This is on DEV for review. Note that while I reprocessed this one icon to show the before/after differences, other icons would not be reprocessed without intervention or a future update to the icon file.
